title: March 24 National Day of Memory, Truth and Justice march in Buenos Aires
location: Buenos Aires; photo report depicts march to Plaza de Mayo. Other locations beyond Buenos Aires not enumerated.
scope: Public march in Buenos Aires on the 48th anniversary of the 1976 coup; report also refers broadly to mobilizations across Argentina without providing a deduplicated nationwide scope.
organizer: Social organizations, unions and political parties (as captioned by El País); named organizers not reviewed.
participants_original: El País subtitle reports “Miles de argentinos” attending the mobilization; a caption says thousands marched toward Plaza de Mayo.
threshold_50_evidence: “Miles de argentinos” and “Miles marchan” explicitly support a public gathering well above 50. Qualitative original wording retained; no numeric estimate inferred.

start_date.summary: El País page date and article title identify March 24, 2024.

location.summary: Photo captions say thousands marched toward Plaza de Mayo; report is El País América, Argentina.

scope.summary: Page is a visual report of the Buenos Aires mobilization; captions mention national mobilizations generally, but locations/counts elsewhere are unverified.

organizer.summary: Caption names social organizations, unions and parties as calling the mobilization.

demands.summary: No state/state-policy target is established by reviewed captions. The article’s contextual description of government position and the additional justice demand do not identify a state addressee; demand remains uncoded and eligibility pending state-target review.

participants_original.summary: Subtitle uses “Miles de argentinos”; caption says “Miles marchan hacia Plaza de Mayo”.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Source’s plural “miles” clearly exceeds 50; no exact count offered.

protester_violence.summary: Unknown; not established by reviewed captions.

state_response.summary: Unknown; not established by reviewed captions.

review_note: The march date, location, organizer, and qualitative attendance are supported by S012. The reviewed captions do not establish a protest demand addressed to the state or state policy. Do not infer the target from contextual descriptions of the government; eligibility remains pending_state_target.
open_questions: Does an admissible source identify any state or state-policy addressee for the memorial march or for the additional justice demand? The reviewed El País captions identify remembrance and a justice demand concerning reported assault/threats but do not name a state actor or policy target; eligibility therefore remains pending_state_target.
What were the march’s onset time and duration/end? The reviewed photo report dates the march to March 24 but does not establish start/end times.

Does the report document only the Buenos Aires march or additional locations that belong to the same episode? Its reviewed captions establish Plaza de Mayo, while any wider geographic scope remains unverified.

Do other exact-URL accounts provide independent confirmation? S012 credits Reuters/AP imagery, so caption syndication and publisher independence require checking before treating another photo report as independent corroboration.

title: International Women’s Day march at Congress in Buenos Aires
location: Plaza de los Dos Congresos / Congress area, Buenos Aires.
scope: Public march and assembly on International Women’s Day; article documents central Buenos Aires gathering. No national count or other locations assumed.
organizer: Organizations that convened the mobilization and agreed on the closing document; article does not enumerate the full coalition.
participants_original: Infobae describes “las miles de mujeres” occupying the public space and a “multitud”; no official or numeric count.
threshold_50_evidence: Source explicitly describes thousands occupying the plaza and public space, well over 50; no exact number inferred.

start_date.summary: The report is explicitly about the 2024 March 8 8M march; text says “hoy” while describing the 8 March march.

location.summary: The source places participants at Plaza de los Dos Congresos and Congress in Buenos Aires.

scope.summary: Story documents central Buenos Aires public march; it does not establish total scope elsewhere.

organizer.summary: Closing document had consensus of several convening organizations, but names are not complete in reviewed section.

demands.summary: Infobae lines 94–107 summarize and quote the closing organizations’ demands: work and against layoffs, wage/minimum-salary and community-cook pay concerns in the context of government adjustment (labor_wage_dispute); opposition to food-price protection deregulation, hunger and cost of necessities (price_increases_tax_policy); sexual/reproductive rights and the anti-protest protocol (social_restrictions); and opposition to the DNU/current government policy (political_behavior_process). These are directly described as demands, not inferred from general grievances.

participants_original.summary: Infobae says “las miles de mujeres se apropian” of the public space and calls it a “multitud”; no numeric attendance estimate.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: “Miles” of participants clearly exceeds the 50-person threshold.

end_date.summary: Duration/end is not established by reviewed article portion.

state_response.summary: Article says police were present and barriers placed, but no complete response dimension adjudicated.

review_note: Four demand categories are retained because the closing document and directly quoted sections support labor/wage, food price/tax policy, social restrictions affecting gender/sexual rights and protest, and political behavior/process. No additional category is inferred.
open_questions: What was the march’s duration/end, and does any admissible source document activity continuing beyond March 8? The reviewed Infobae report describes the March 8 event but does not establish an end date or later continuation.

What concrete state responses, if any, followed the gathering? Infobae describes police presence and barriers but the reviewed account does not establish arrests, beatings, dispersal, accommodation, killings or shootings.

Does any other exact-URL account independently corroborate the event and demand statements? Infobae is the only body currently used; the Buenos Aires Times lead remains search-only and its independence/body scope are unreviewed.

Does the episode share an organizer, demand sequence or continuing activity with another March event? No reviewed evidence establishes a cross-date episode link; keep the event separate unless usable reporting establishes continuity.
